tagline: On-site power for the AI era, built on solid oxide fuel cells
hero_kpi_rationale: Product revenue is the most direct measure of the volume of fuel cells delivered and accepted: twenty-six quarters taken verbatim from the company's income statements, from $99.6 million in the first quarter of 2020 to $935.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, more than ninefold. Until 2023 the company published megawatts accepted (268 MW in 2023, 1,241 MW cumulative), a still more telling metric, but it stopped doing so from the fiscal 2024 annual report onwards: that series ends in 2023 and now sits in the Stories block. Product revenue takes over without a break and stays current.

kpis.name: Product revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the sale of Energy Server fuel cell systems, recognised at customer acceptance.
kpis.description: Twenty-six quarters of history, from $99.6 million in Q1 2020 to $935.4 million in Q2 2026.
kpis.signal: Product revenue reached $935.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 215% year over year from $296.6 million. It is the most direct measure of the volume of fuel cells delivered and accepted, the company having stopped publishing megawatts accepted after 2023.

kpis.name: Product gross margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin on Energy Server hardware sales, as published by the company.
kpis.description: Five fiscal years, from 29% in 2021 to 35% in 2025.
kpis.signal: Published product gross margin moved from 29% in 2021 to 37% in 2024 then back to 35% in 2025 as the manufacturing ramp absorbed part of the unit gain. It is the only durably profitable line of the income statement.

kpis.name: Service revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from five to twenty year operations and maintenance contracts attached to the installed base.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from $95.8 million in 2019 to $228.3 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Service revenue rose from $95.8 million in 2019 to $228.3 million in 2025 and turned profitable in 2025, at a 10% gross margin, after four loss-making years.

kpis.name: Installation revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from engineering, permitting, construction and commissioning of Energy Server sites.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from $60.8 million in 2019 to $204.1 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Installation revenue jumped 66.8% in 2025 to $204.1 million after five flat years. The company attributes this to project milestone timing on sites with tight time-to-power commitments. The line remains just below breakeven, at -1% gross margin.

kpis.name: Electricity revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from electricity sold under power purchase agreements on company-operated systems.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from $71.2 million in 2019 to $60.4 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Electricity revenue has stayed between $53 million and $82 million since 2019 and now accounts for only 3% of the total, against 9% in 2019. Its gross margin went from -117% in 2023, the year of the PPA V repowering, to 46% in 2025.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.explanation: Consolidated quarterly revenue, all revenue types combined.
kpis.description: Twenty-two quarters of history, from $194.0 million in Q1 2021 to $1,065.4 million in Q2 2026.
kpis.signal: Quarterly revenue passed one billion dollars for the first time in the second quarter of 2026, at $1,065.4 million, up 165.5% year over year. The company raised full year 2026 guidance to a $3.9 to $4.2 billion range.

kpis.name: Total gross margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin across all four revenue types.
kpis.description: Five fiscal years, from 20% in 2021 to 29% in 2025.
kpis.signal: Published total gross margin recovered from 12% in 2022, a year weighted down by the write-off of legacy servers, to 29% in 2025, and reached 33.4% in the second quarter of 2026, an all-time high.

kpis.name: Operating income (loss)
kpis.explanation: Consolidated operating result before non-operating items and tax.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from -$232.8 million in 2019 to $72.8 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Operating income turned positive in 2024 for the first time in the company's history, at $22.9 million, then reached $72.8 million in 2025 after a low of -$261.0 million in 2022. The second quarter of 2026 alone delivered $182.2 million.

kpis.name: Research and development expense
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from $104.2 million in 2019 to $186.0 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: The company spent a record $186.0 million on research and development in 2025 after a pause at $148.6 million in 2024. That is 9.2% of revenue against 13.3% in 2019: spending is growing more slowly than sales.

kpis.name: Cash flow from operating activities
kpis.explanation: Net cash provided by or used in operating activities.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from $163.8 million in 2019 to $113.9 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Operating cash flow turned positive again in 2024 at $92.0 million then $113.9 million in 2025, after a $372.5 million outflow in 2023 tied to inventory build. The second quarter of 2026 alone brought in $226.4 million.

kpis.name: Full-time employees
kpis.explanation: Full-time headcount worldwide at fiscal year end.
kpis.description: Six fiscal years, from 1,316 in 2020 to 2,214 in 2025.
kpis.signal: The company had 2,214 full-time employees at the end of 2025, of which 1,752 in the United States and 395 in India, after a peak of 2,530 at the end of 2022. Revenue per employee rose from $0.53 million in 2021 to $0.91 million in 2025.

kpis.name: Product share of revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of total revenue coming from hardware sales.
kpis.description: Seven fiscal years, from 71.0% in 2019 to 75.7% in 2025.
kpis.signal: Hardware accounted for 75.7% of revenue in 2025 and rises to 87.8% in the second quarter of 2026. The model is that of an equipment maker selling machines, not that of a power producer: the electricity share has fallen to 3%.

stories_kpis.name: Product accepted (100 kW systems)
stories_kpis.explanation: Number of Energy Server customer acceptances, measured in 100 kilowatt equivalents.
stories_kpis.description: Five fiscal years, from 1,194 in 2019 to 2,682 in 2023. Discontinued after 2023.
stories_kpis.signal: The company accepted 2,682 hundred-kilowatt equivalent systems in 2023 against 1,194 in 2019, a steady 22% a year. It stopped publishing this metric from the fiscal 2024 annual report onwards, so the series stops at the end of 2023 and product revenue takes over.

stories_kpis.name: Megawatts accepted, net
stories_kpis.explanation: Annual net capacity accepted by customers.
stories_kpis.description: Three fiscal years, from 188 MW in 2021 to 268 MW in 2023. Discontinued after 2023.
stories_kpis.signal: Net acceptances moved from 188 MW in 2021 to 268 MW in 2023. The fiscal 2023 annual report states those 268 MW lifted cumulative megawatts accepted from 973 to 1,241 MW. Publication stopped after 2023.

stories_kpis.name: Cumulative megawatts accepted, net
stories_kpis.explanation: Total capacity accepted by customers since inception.
stories_kpis.description: Two fiscal years, 973 MW in 2022 and 1,241 MW in 2023. Discontinued after 2023.
stories_kpis.signal: Cumulative megawatts accepted reached 1,241 MW at the end of 2023 against 973 MW a year earlier. This installed base feeds service revenue, which runs on five to twenty year maintenance contracts.

stories_kpis.name: Deployed base in South Korea
stories_kpis.explanation: Energy Server capacity deployed in the Republic of Korea.
stories_kpis.description: Two fiscal years, nearly 600 MW in 2024 and nearly 682 MW in 2025.
stories_kpis.signal: South Korea, the company's second market opened in 2018, reached nearly 682 MW of deployed systems at the end of 2025 against nearly 600 MW a year earlier, through distribution partnerships with SK ecoplant and SK eternix.

stories_kpis.name: U.S. revenue share
stories_kpis.explanation: Share of total revenue generated in the United States.
stories_kpis.description: Four fiscal years, from 56% in 2022 to 81% in 2025.
stories_kpis.signal: The United States accounted for 81% of revenue in 2025 against 56% in 2022, a year in which most revenue came from South Korea. The shift follows North American data centre demand.

stories_kpis.name: Largest customer share of revenue
stories_kpis.explanation: Share of total revenue taken by the single largest contractual counterparty.
stories_kpis.description: Three fiscal years, 37% in 2023, 23% in 2024 and 43% in 2025.
stories_kpis.signal: The largest customer accounted for 43% of revenue in 2025 against 23% in 2024 and 37% in 2023. The company states this counterparty is a related party and that, for this disclosure, customer means the contractual counterparty, which may be a project finance vehicle rather than the end user.

stories_kpis.name: PhDs in the R&D team
stories_kpis.explanation: Number of doctorate holders in the research organisation.
stories_kpis.signal: The research team includes 62 PhDs in materials science and in electrical, chemical, mechanical, civil and nuclear engineering at the end of 2025. The company states it has more than two and a half times extended fuel cell life since its first generation.

risks.title: Growing dependence on AI data centre demand
risks.description: The company states that its AI-linked customer mix is increasing and that a slowdown, real or perceived, in data centre deployment would adversely affect its business, financial condition and results.
risks.score_rationale: Fourth bullet of the risk factor summary in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report, and absent from the fiscal 2023 edition: the risk is new and rising fast. The numbers confirm it: the largest customer accounted for 43% of revenue in 2025 and 2026 guidance assumes a doubling of revenue entirely tied to this outlet.

risks.title: Extreme customer concentration
risks.description: In fiscal 2025, three customers accounted for approximately 43%, 13% and 12% of revenue, the first being a related party. On receivables, the same three counterparties represent 41%, 17% and 15%.
risks.score_rationale: Figures taken verbatim from the Concentration of Risk note in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report: 68% of revenue on three counterparties, 73% of receivables on the same. The largest customer's weight nearly doubled in a year, from 23% in 2024. The risk is immediate and measured, hence the maximum score.

risks.title: Production capacity ramp
risks.description: The company states that its future growth depends in part on its ability to increase production capacity for its products, and that it has limited experience manufacturing new products.
risks.score_rationale: Opening risk of the Risks Related to Our Products and Manufacturing chapter of the company's fiscal 2025 annual report. Made concrete by guidance implying a doubling of revenue in 2026 and by the $69.3 million rise in receivables and contract assets tied to milestone billing on several large late-year deployments.

risks.title: Dependence on tax credits and public incentive programmes
risks.description: The business currently benefits from rebates, tax credits and other public financial programmes, and changes to them could cause revenue to decline. The company cites the Section 48C credit of up to $75.3 million, whose disbursement remains subject to certification conditions and administrative clearance.
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated risk chapter in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report, with a quantified amount and an explicitly described administrative freeze on the disbursement of Inflation Reduction Act funds. Direct financial reach but bounded against $2,024 million of revenue.

risks.title: Supply chain and sole-source suppliers
risks.description: The company and some of its suppliers obtain capital equipment and components from sole suppliers; unavailability would delay deliveries. It also flags supply chain competition and purchase commitments that can create excess or insufficient inventory.
risks.score_rationale: Four separate bullets of the risk factor summary in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report concern supply, making it the most repeated theme of the chapter. Materialised by the inventory build ahead of anticipated 2026 demand.

risks.title: High upfront costs and reliance on third-party financiers
risks.description: The company's products carry significant upfront costs and, for some customers, it must attract financiers to help fund purchases. It states that its ability to deploy its backlog is directly tied to securing project financing, a process it calls unpredictable.
risks.score_rationale: Third bullet of the risk factor summary in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report, stated without conditional wording on the link between financing and deployment. Counterweight: the August 2025 financing framework with Brookfield Asset Management, described in the same document.

risks.title: Long sales and installation cycle, and competition
risks.description: The company states that its products involve a lengthy sales and installation cycle and that failing to close sales on a regular timely basis would harm its business; it also faces significant competition, citing small modular nuclear reactors and gas turbines.
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk present in every annual report since the IPO, so nothing new. Partly defused by the fiscal 2025 report itself, which notes an increasing number of transactions moving from booking to revenue in less than twelve months.

risks.title: Tariffs and grid interconnection requirements
risks.description: The company states that trade tariffs could have a material adverse effect on its business, and that deployment of its fuel cells depends on interconnection requirements, export tariff arrangements and utility tariff requirements, all subject to change.
risks.score_rationale: Two bullets of the risk factor summary in the company's fiscal 2025 annual report. Real exposure given the foreign trade zone used to import components, but the company manufactures most of its systems in the United States, which bounds the effect.

governance.notes: Single class of Class A common stock, one share one vote. The 21 May 2026 annual meeting approved removal of the inoperative Class B common stock provisions, struck from the charter on 26 May 2026. Founder KR Sridhar serves as both chairman and chief executive; a lead independent director is designated by the independent directors. Nine of ten directors are independent, three are women. 2025 CEO total compensation of $3.5 million, a 35.6 to 1 pay ratio, and say-on-pay approval of 96.3%.

ai_positioning.summary: Bloom Energy builds neither models nor chips: it sells the on-site electricity that powers AI data centres. Its solid oxide fuel cells connect in months where a grid connection takes years, which has shifted its market from commercial buildings to compute operators in two years.
evidence: Second quarter 2026 earnings release: the founder and chief executive states that all major US hyperscalers and over a dozen US neoclouds, AI labs and colocation data centre operators have validated and approved the company's power solutions for their AI factories, and that Bloom is now a standard for AI onsite power.
Fiscal 2025 annual report, risk factor summary: a dedicated risk factor states that the AI customer mix is increasing and that slower data centre expansion would adversely affect the business.

Fiscal 2025 annual report: a one gigawatt supply agreement signed with American Electric Power, including an initial 100 MW order placed in 2024; the company states it began deploying projects across that utility's territory in 2025.

Figures: product revenue moved from $226.3 million in the second quarter of 2024 to $935.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, more than fourfold in two years, and 2026 guidance was raised to $3.9 to $4.2 billion, a doubling at the midpoint.

Fiscal 2025 annual report: work on emerging data centre power architectures, notably 800 volt direct current systems, and on load-following for grid-independent microgrids supporting data centre environments.

events.title: First quarter above one billion dollars and raised full year guidance
events.description: The company reports quarterly revenue of $1,065.4 million, up 165.5% year over year, gross margin of 33.4% and operating income of $182.2 million, and raises 2026 guidance to a $3.9 to $4.2 billion range (source: exhibit to the Form 8-K filed 28 July 2026).

events.title: Annual meeting: charter amended and pay approved at 96.3%
events.description: Shareholders approve removal of the Class B common stock provisions and officer exculpation as permitted by Delaware law; executive compensation receives 96.3% support (source: Form 8-K filed 27 May 2026).

events.title: First fiscal year above two billion dollars of revenue
events.description: The fiscal 2025 annual report shows revenue of $2,024.0 million, up 37.3%, gross margin of 29% and operating income of $72.8 million, a second consecutive year in the black (source: Form 10-K filed 9 February 2026).

events.title: Financing framework concluded with Brookfield Asset Management
events.description: The company concludes a transaction with Brookfield Asset Management, flagged by its auditor as a critical audit matter under investments in unconsolidated affiliates; the arrangement is intended to fund project deployment (source: fiscal 2025 annual report).
